summary: `expenses itemizations`, `reports exceptions` and `expenses update --type` are MCP tools that run the companion CLI, and a regen must keep them reachable from MCP.
reason: The Cobra-tree mirror skips pp:endpoint commands on the assumption that a typed tool covers them, and an in-process typed tool needs a registered platform source for its fresh-tenant gate, which this CLI has none of, so a hand-added endpoint command was unreachable from MCP. The tools run the CLI and own the gate as child-CLI tools; the type edit has to go through the CLI because the API rejects expense writes for browser-session auth.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: In-process typed MCP tools for a CLI with no registered platform source
deferred_to_upstream.reason: requireFreshTenantGate fails closed when VerifyMCPInvocation yields no session, so every in-process typed tool of this CLI (expenses_get, reports_list, ...) answers "MCP tenant gate is not configured". That is generator policy for CLIs without a platform source and belongs upstream; once it is fixed, typed tools for these endpoints can replace the CLI-routed ones.

validated_outcome: go build, go vet and go test ./... pass. Unit tests cover registration (child-CLI gate owner, read-only hints, schemas), the exact CLI argv including flag-like values, input validation without running the CLI, a failing CLI and a missing CLI. Verified end to end over MCP stdio with the real concur-pp-mcp and concur-pp-cli binaries against a fake Concur server and a fake agent-browser: both reads hit the expected paths, a type the picker does not offer stops unsaved and returns the offered list, and an offered type completes. Not exercised against a real tenant through MCP.
